questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical OS I/O scheduling knowledge, device heterogeneity, and fairness under mixed workloads. It requires concrete data structures and a concrete scheduling policy.

## Key Concepts
- Block I/O scheduling and per-device queues
- Priority-aware fairness across heterogeneous devices
- Read/write path optimization and deadline vs throughput trade-offs
- Data structures: per-device heaps/queues, per-process weights

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-C-like sketch
typedef struct IOReq { int pid; int type; int prio; int deadline; int addr; int len; } IOReq;
typedef struct DeviceQueue { Heap reads; Heap writes; int device_id; } DeviceQueue;
IOReq* pick_next(DeviceQueue* dq) { /* if has reads, pop min by deadline; else pop writes by addr */ }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate fairness under bursty mixed workloads?
- How to adjust dynamically when SSD queue depth changes or new devices hot-plugged?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of crash-safe metadata updates and recovery in a simple FS. It exercises correctness under failures, not just performance.

## Key Concepts

- Write-ahead logs for metadata
- Atomic directory operations
- Two-phase commit and idempotent replay
- Crash recovery test strategies

## Code Example

```c
// Minimal sketch for log append/commit
typedef struct LogRecord { uint64_t txid; uint8_t type; uint32_t inode; uint32_t dirent; uint32_t len; } LogRecord;
int log_append(LogRecord *r, void *payload, size_t plen);
int commit_tx(uint64_t txid);
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How to guarantee recoverability if power fails after commit but before applying changes?
- How would you test recovery across crashes?
